strips.hook: [device: ritual-as-agency] [target: the protagonists' own failings | form: two-hander | aim: inward | mechanic: anti-work-equilibrium | cast: Milo+Cal] You refresh the inbox that would have pinged you anyway - not for the reply, for the one thing at work that responds the second you ask. (2-panel recut: the 3-panel original was killed under S13, user 2026-08-02 - the reveal closed in panel 2 and panel 3 topped it.)
strips.caption: The button is the only one that answers.

strips.hook: [device: baseline-arbitrage] [target: comp plan & quota | form: three-hander (witness) | aim: inward | mechanic: perverse-incentive-harvest / baseline-arbitrage variant | cast: Diane+Milo+Cal] Territory reshuffle. The new SDR thanks Cal for leaving him the big patch; Cal asked for the small one, because next year's quota comes off last year's number, not the map.
strips.caption:
Nobody's quota comes off the map.

Next year's number is built from what the patch did last year — which makes the best territory in the room the most expensive one to own. The new guy always picks the big one.

strips.hook: [device: label-arbitrage] [target: cross-functional friction | form: two-hander | aim: lateral | mechanic: perverse-incentive-harvest (a respected LABEL is manufactured, not a metric) | cast: Maren+Susie — no Cal, no HOBS, no authority figure] In a sales company the only immovable calendar object is a customer, so marketing's real writing hour is booked as a customer call. Radar seed: HN 'Prevent cognitive debt by manually retyping LLM-generated code' (403 up / 342 comments) — thematic only (deliberately protecting slow work from a system that erodes it); Reddit was unreachable in today's radar, so no confessed-behavior calendar thread was available.
strips.caption: Marketing's queue is six weeks. The thing everyone waits six weeks for is two numbers in a headline — and nobody has read past them since 2019.

strips.hook: [device: planted-concession] [target: deal desk & discounting | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: illusion-demolition | cast: Frank+Milo] Clause Eleven — the CFO wrote a losable clause into the paper so the buyer's lawyer spends his one deletion directly above the auto-renewal. Radar seed: Lobsters 'Kill the Cookie Banner' (137up) — the confessed behaviour of accepting terms unread.
strips.caption:
Somewhere in that contract is the one line that exists to be deleted.

Every legal review has to produce a redline. Somebody on the vendor side decided in advance what it would be.

strips.hook: [device: expiry-as-close] [target: customers and prospects | form: presentation (group scene, ONE speaker) | aim: outward | mechanic: dependency-as-deadline (weaponised literalism of the buyer's own "evaluation") | cast: Cal + Diane + Roz — Roz's debut in the bank, Cal is the only speaker] Day 118 of a thirty-day trial: the account was never stalled, it is already in production — so the tenth polite nudge is a service-termination notice. NOT a two-hander (ledger: 7/9 of the bank), outward aim (scarcest at 1/9), first presentation form and first one-speaker strip in the bank.
strips.caption:
Day 118 of a thirty-day trial.

They were never stalled — their board deck already runs on your free account. That deal does not need a decision. It needs an expiry date.

strips.hook: [device: process-recursion] [target: bureaucratic process | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: policy-as-punchline | cast: Milo+Frank] The cheap purchase is the slow one — the fix is to spend more. Standalone; references nothing outside its own three panels. Scored 29/30 by independent craft judges in two separate rounds and passed the cold-scroller gate in both.

[device: engineered-error] [target: cross-functional friction | form: two-hander | aim: lateral | mechanic: perverse-incentive-harvest | cast: Susie+Maren] Marketing catches a wrong stat in Susie's follow-up to a silent prospect. The error is the instrument: a prospect who can ignore a question cannot ignore a mistake, so every email she sends has exactly one number wrong.
strips.caption:
You cannot make a prospect answer you. You can make them correct you.

Susie's follow-ups all have exactly one thing wrong with them. Marketing found out this morning.

strips.hook: [device: public-thanks-as-deposit] [target: performance reviews | form: three-hander (pull-back witness) | aim: inward | mechanic: ritual-with-a-hidden-invoice | cast: Cal+Susie+Maren] Self-assessment week: the entire written record of your appreciation is two search hits, and the one compliment in writing came from the colleague who does it on purpose.
strips.caption: Nine months of work, two search results. Self-assessment season is the week you discover that praise said out loud does not exist. Cal worked this out a long time ago.

strips.hook: [device: measurement-date-arbitrage] [target: vendors & procurement | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: perverse-incentive-harvest | cast: Frank+Susie] Susie's seat in the sales tool dies at nine. Frank released twelve before Friday's renewal quote — and tells her to come back Monday and ask for two.
strips.caption:
Your seat didn't break. It got quoted.

Renewal pricing counts the seats switched on, not the people logging in — so twelve go dark before Friday and come back Monday.

strips.hook: [device: compliance-laundering] [target: vendors & procurement | form: two-hander | aim: outward | mechanic: weaponised-literalism | cast: Frank+Susie] Susie needs a $1,240 tool only one vendor makes. The three-quote rule looks unsatisfiable without lying — so Frank, who enforces it, tells her to ask the vendor she already chose for its own competitor sheet: two real names, priced to lose.
strips.caption:
One vendor makes it. Three quotes required.
